subject: Request: tiered rate + market protection approval for Novanet deal
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Ariel Soto <ariel.soto@novanet.com>; Procurement <procurement@novanet.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: tiered rate + market protection for Q3 pilot (Novanet)

Ariel / team — thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Novanet is prepared to commit to a 12-month pilot across their intelligence platform (estimated 600M tokens/mo at peak). They indicated pricing sensitivity and also asked for some market-protection language.

Attached: SOW draft and a short risk summary (see Novanet_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood_risk_summary.xlsx). High-level commercial ask from Novanet: 
- Tiered effective rate: $0.0009 per gen-token for months 1–3, $0.0007 months 4–9, $0.0006 months 10–12 (volume thresholds tied to MAU).
- A 12-month "market protection" clause: Novanet wants right-to-match / price-parity vs any comparable vendor offers targeted at the Healthcare vertical in North America for the duration of the pilot (they phrased as a competitive-protection/MFN-like commitment).
- A narrow exclusivity ask: they requested we not engage certain named competitors for targeted enterprise programs in Healthcare for 6 months.

We can trade deeper near-term discounts for controls on duration/scope. I think a workable commercial compromise would be: tiered rate above, limited price-protection tied to audited volume bands (not open-ended MFN), explicit carveouts for public sector and channel partners, and a 6-month review/sunset on any market-protection benefit.

Asking: Legal / Deal Desk / Sales leadership — need guidance and explicit approval path for (A) any MFN/right-to-match language, and (B) any exclusivity/market-restriction. Novanet needs an answer by EOD Friday (they're in procurement cycle).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

—
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Mike — quick read and initial redlines below. Quoting your note for context:

> Attached: SOW draft and a short risk summary... High-level commercial ask from Novanet: 
> - Tiered effective rate...
> - A 12-month "market protection" clause...
> - A narrow exclusivity ask...

Concise legal perspective: 
1) MFN / price-parity: broad MFN clauses are high risk — they can retroactively require us to change pricing across customers and conflict with committed promotional/partner pricing. We could consider a limited price-review/price-match right but it must be: (a) timeboxed (<= 6 months), (b) scope-limited to the exact SKU/region, (c) subject to audit rights and a cap on retroactive remediation, and (d) exclude marketplace/channel/partner offers.
2) Exclusivity/market partition: we cannot grant exclusive market rights to entire verticals or regions. We can offer: capacity prioritization, dedicated support, or "preferred supplier" status limited to a named product line and a narrow set of named competitors, for a defined term. Any language that restricts our ability to sell to a segment will require Exec/Legal sign-off and a compensating commercial concession.
3) Reporting/volume audit: if price protections are offered, insist on quarterly volume reconciliation and a $/token true-up mechanism (with a capped liability).

Please provide: a redline SOW with proposed alternate clause language (I can draft but will need deal specifics). If Sales wants MFN-like protection, escalate to Rishi + Lauren for Deal Desk approval; if either approves, I will draft controlled alternatives (sunset, carveouts, liability cap).

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Appreciate the summary. From a deals perspective: I am comfortable with the tiered rates proposed by Mike as long as Finance signs off on the projected blended unit economics — I'll coordinate with Finance this afternoon.

On the market-protection and exclusivity asks: I will not approve a unilateral MFN or blanket exclusivity. Acceptable compromise for commercial approval: 
- Limited benchmark protection: price-parity right that only applies to competing direct-enterprise proposals in the Healthcare vertical within North America, capped at the pilot term, and subject to quarterly reconciliation. No retroactive reopening beyond a fixed $250k cap in remedial credits.
- Exclusivity: only permissible as a narrowly-scoped "preferred" arrangement tied to the Novanet clinical-workflow product; must exclude public sector and pre-existing channel partners. Term = 6 months with automatic sunset unless re-approved.

If Legal (Marissa) can produce redline language that reflects the caps/sunsets and excludes marketplaces, I will provisionally approve and will escalate to the Exec review only if Finance flags material margin erosion. Lauren — please confirm Deal Desk acceptance of the proposed caps and whether the $250k remedial cap is reasonable operationally.

Rishi
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
